title: Onprem network heisenbugs - weekly digest
body:
Purpose:
Weekly standup + incident digest focused on a set of flaky networking issues customers are seeing during onprem/VPC installs. This is a working summary for the field + SRE + install engineers.

High-level summary:
- Several customers reported intermittent agent <-> gateway disconnects that manifest as 5-30s stalls in model responses.
- Root-cause appears to be a set of related but non-identical network symptoms: MTU blackholes, asymmetric routing causing TCP resets, and occasional iBGP session flaps on customer routers.
- Repro is intermittent; we have one customer (Customer-F) with a deterministic repro when large batched payloads hit a path through an older firewall.
- Immediate mitigations: reduce default batch size for affected customers, pin fallback to hosted for critical routes, and push a short-term MTU probe during handshake.

Standup notes (this week):
Mon 2026-11-09:
- Field reported two installs with stalls (Customer-F, Customer-R). Packet captures taken (pcap-2741-custF.pcap).
- Action: ask customer network team to mirror path to our lab for controlled repro (Amira + Customer-F).

Tue 2026-11-10:
- Lab observed retransmit spikes when payloads > 1200B and PMTU discovery suppressed by firewall. Suspect PMTUD drop.
- Quick test: lowering agent MTU from 1500 -> 1400 reduced stalls in lab. Verified with ci-echo load test.
- Ticket JIRA-2741 created to track MTU mitigation across fleet.

Wed 2026-11-11 (Network sync):
- SRE joined to review BGP logs; found repeated TCP session resets on iBGP neighbor at customer edge around times of high burst. Noted customer router running older IOS with known bug (see linked Confluence).
- Decided: recommend customer upgrade; while blocked, implement software-side keepalive and exponential backoff of reconnects.

Thu 2026-11-12 (Install clinic):
- Dmitri paired with field to walk through firewall rule list; found a deep-inspection rule that rewrites TCP MSS on SYN in a nonstandard way. This explained PMTUD failures.
- Workaround: add explicit MSS clamp on our tunnel endpoint and add inline MTU probe during TLS handshake to detect rewrite.

Fri 2026-11-13 (Customer handoff):
- Customer-F accepted temporary MSS clamp; latency improved and stalls dropped from 3/day -> 0-1/day.
- Customer-R could not change firewall rules; reverting to hosted fallback for certain high-p99 workloads (JIRA-2798).

What we tried (technical details):
- Packet captures and Wireshark analysis: looked for ICMP type 3 code 4 (frag needed) messages and found suppression for two customers.
- Implemented a small experiment in agent: send explicit UDP-style MTU probe during TLS setup and log response. Non-invasive and quick to roll out as a flag.
- MSS clamp: kernel-level iptables/netfilter rule that sets TCP MSS to 1400 on tunnel interfaces. Requires admin rights on customer host.
- Keepalive/backoff: toggled from aggressive 5s retry to exponential 1s->2s->4s up to 32s; reduced load on crushed customer routers.

Open blockers (priority ordered):
- JIRA-2741: customer consent for MSS clamp on 4 remaining installs. (Owner: Amira)
- JIRA-2798: define fallback policy for customers that cannot modify firewalls (Owner: Priya). Need SRE signoff on safety of fallback and cost estimate.
- Waiting on Customer-T to provide router debug logs for iBGP flaps (Owner: Liaison-ops).

Decisions made this week:
- Default agent batch size for onprem installs affected by MTU regression will be reduced by 25% under a temporary flag. Rollout window: next 48 hours to all installs marked as 'at risk'.
- Add an optional MTU probe at handshake as a feature flagged opt-in; default off. Will move to on by default if no negative impact after 2 weeks.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Amira: finalize MSS clamp instructions and one-click curl commands for customers; ETA 2026-11-20.
- Liu: instrument agent to emit MTU probe logs and add toggles to console; ETA 2026-11-17 (deploy canary).
- Dmitri: produce an install checklist entry for firewall deep-inspection rules and MSS issues; ETA 2026-11-19.
- Priya: draft fallback billing and routing policy for hosted fallback and present to product on 2026-11-23.
- SRE (assigned): run safety review of exponential backoff change (link to PR-882).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider an agent-level active path test that runs outside request path (like periodic mini-requests) to detect client-visible PMTUD suppression early and auto-flip small-batch mode.
- We should capture eBPF metrics on customer hosts (where allowed) to inspect MSS clamp behavior without asking for full packet captures.
- Explore whether we can detect deep-inspection firewalls via TLS fingerprint anomalies during handshake.

Customer updates to send this week (skeleton):
- Customer-F: confirm MSS clamp improved perf; propose scheduled window to make clamp permanent or revert after upgrade.
- Customer-R: propose limited hosted fallback and bill-impact estimate; recommend firewall vendor ticket escalation.

Meeting log excerpts:
- 2026-11-11 14:00 Network Sync: "If we can detect PMTUD suppression in 1s we avoid whole-class of stalls" - SRE Lead.
- 2026-11-12 10:30 Install Clinic: "Customer firewalls are the real wild west, document every checkbox." - Dmitri.

Attachments / artifacts kept in folder (internal reference):
- pcap-2741-custF.pcap
- mtuprobes-canary-2026-11-16.log
- PR-882 (keepalive/backoff) diff

Risks and concerns:
- Some customers will be unwilling/unable to change host-level iptables; we need a robust, low-cost fallback for them.
- Rolling out MSS clamps broadly without customer consent could break other middleboxes — need clear opt-in/out and strong rollout monitoring.

Next week focus:
- Canary MTU probe to 10 installs (Liu) and validate false-positive rate < 2%.
- Complete MSS clamp invitation flow + install consent (Amira).
- Finalize fallback policy and cost impact for product review (Priya).

If you have extra cycles: pull logs for Customer-T and run a comparative BGP neighbor stability test against lab router (script: tools/bgp-stress.sh).

End of digest.

(rough / notes-style doc — will clean to a formal playbook once blockers are closed)
